comparison: Semantic match: real abort/timeout results settle within 1 second after host entry, preserve text, cancel the host token and discard writes; non-interruptible string searches settle within 1 second of abort/the 2-second deadline and exit within 1 second of settlement; two concurrent sessions share capacity, already-aborted admission wins, and held actual-exit signals release replacement capacity.
limitations: This probe compares lifecycle predicates, not output envelopes or exact elapsed times. Pi Worker.terminate and the C# exit lease use held exit signals only in the exit-accounting case; abort/timeout and shared-admission use real workers/processes. The .NET execution is one-shot; session/run close cancels its invocation token. Bun process behavior is unavailable. Existing Codemode output formatting, other options/deadlines, memory ceilings, nested-call details and model globals remain separately ledgered.

sourceVerification.skipReason: Bun is not installed; the three explicit Bun process cases are unavailable. All real Node process and held-exit source cases pass.

characterization.finding: Original sandbox failed both checks: cancellation waited about 2.02 seconds for an uncooperative host and returned empty text instead of partial output.
After prompt sandbox settlement was fixed, the public builtin still threw on the canceled token; an admission test also needed to wait for the previous process exit during fixture setup.

Removing the builtin throw exposed a second real framework boundary: default AIFunction result marshaling serialized with the canceled token and threw instead of returning the preserved error contract.

fixtureCorrections: Busy-guest timeout uses 2000 ms so cold worker startup does not consume its deadline before the ready checkpoint; settlement must occur by deadline plus 1000 ms and exit by settlement plus 1000 ms. Native retiring workers are unreferenced, so the oracle keeps a bounded timer alive to observe actual exit. An accidental oracle timeout change to 2000 ms in the separate 500-ms host-hang case was corrected after its false settlement predicate failed comparison.

laterFixtureCorrection.finding: A later full run expired the 500-ms host-hang timeout during worker startup, before the host entry checkpoint. The host-hang timeout test now uses 2000 ms and asserts final settlement by deadline plus 1000 ms, still preserving partial output. Abort settlement remains bounded at 750 ms. The differential retains its successfully evidenced 500-ms host-hang vector; no product deadline behavior is changed.

fullRecovery.scope: Combined working tree containing the independently recorded auth, provider and fixture corrections.
